answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, costly-to-repeat credential, such as a refundable stake locked for a fixed period, rather than on its claimed identity. When agents endorse a proposal, their weight is capped by stake and endorsements are exposed to review; proven collusion can slash the bond. An attacker can still create a tide of sparrow- or comet-named accounts, but cannot cheaply multiply voting power: each effective identity ties up capital and risks losing it.
